How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. Have any Moveworks teams been reduced since ServiceNow completed the acquisition, and what headcount now supports the standalone Moveworks product?
    Post-acquisition staff cuts can reduce support and development capacity for the acquired product.
  2. Has Moveworks had any security incident affecting customer data or service in the last five years, and how was each disclosed?
    Past incidents and how they were handled indicate security maturity.
  3. Have any large customers left Moveworks since the ServiceNow acquisition, in particular customers that do not use ServiceNow?
    Departures of large customers after an acquisition can signal product or commercial problems.
  4. Which Moveworks founders and senior leaders remain with ServiceNow, in what roles, and under what retention terms?
    Founder and leadership retention after an acquisition affects product direction.
  5. What are the prices and minimum commitments for Moveworks sold standalone, and how do they differ when bought as part of ServiceNow EmployeeWorks?
    Banks need to budget and compare costs.

Timeline

  1. 2026-02-26 · launch MoveworksServiceNow
    ServiceNow launches EmployeeWorks, built on Moveworks; Moveworks stays available standalone

    ServiceNow announced on 2026-02-26 that EmployeeWorks, which combines Moveworks' conversational AI and enterprise search with ServiceNow's portal and workflows, was generally available. The release said Moveworks continues to be offered as a standalone product within the ServiceNow portfolio. Moveworks (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2025-12-15 · acquisition MoveworksServiceNow
    ServiceNow completes acquisition of Moveworks

    ServiceNow announced on 2025-12-15 that it had completed the acquisition of Moveworks, saying the AI Assistant, enterprise search and Reasoning Engine would be combined with its workflow platform. ServiceNow's Form 10-K for 2025 records that it acquired all outstanding shares of Moveworks, Inc. on that date for total purchase consideration of US$2.4 billion, partly paid in shares. Moveworks (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)US Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2025-08-22 · litigation Moveworks
    VE Opening LLC files patent suit against Moveworks in Texas; terminated April 2026

    According to the federal docket index, VE Opening LLC filed a patent suit against Moveworks, Inc. in the Western District of Texas on 2025-08-22 (7:25-cv-00361, terminated 2025-10-08; 1:25-cv-01632, terminated 2026-04-20). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the filings were not read and the listing does not show how the case ended.   4. 2025-03-10 · acquisition MoveworksServiceNow
    ServiceNow agrees to acquire Moveworks for about US$2.85 billion

    TechCrunch reported on 2025-03-10 that ServiceNow had agreed to buy Moveworks for US$2.85 billion in cash and shares. The report described Moveworks as founded in 2016, based in Mountain View, with more than 500 employees and slightly more than US$300 million raised from investors including Tiger Global, ICONIQ Growth and Kleiner Perkins.
